newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude firmer, March Tapis said traded higher.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude firmer, March Tapis said traded higher.

text.p: Asian crude prices were firmer on Friday in line with strong futures, as a producer said it has sold March Tapis at quotes +$1.30/+$1.40.

The producer said the 650,000-barrel deal took place "a couple of days ago," indicating it could relate to a Thai refiner's requirements, some sources said, although the producer declined to disclose the buyer.
Traders had said the refiner bought Tapis for March at OSP flat. The producer said it was now offering Tapis at up to $1.45.
Traders were shaping up for the Indian March crude tender, which was expected to be awarded later on Friday.
Traders said about five Dubai cargoes had been offered, with the lowest offer at first-half March quotes plus 43 cents.
Five companies offered VLCCs of Qua Iboe and a trader offered Gulf of Suez at OSP less five cents, traders said.
A European major offered a VLCC of Palanca.
Crude paper spreads were firm in late afternoon. Only bids were seen on Brent/Dubai for March at $2.08, April at $2.00 and May at $1.95, up five cents from earlier in the day.
